tier_reason: Issue #128563 (first-party, Ken Jin) compares the tail-calling build against the default computed-goto build on pyperformance with clang-19, ThinLTO and PGO, and its correction notice gives the 3-5% geomean; benchmark code (pyperformance) is public but no CPU model is stated on the issue or in the linked gist, so it falls short of A. The only independent measurement found (Nelson Elhage's blog) is blocked here and known from search snippets only.

corrections.claimed_speedup: After correction: geomean 3-5% faster on pyperformance (issue correction notice; Python 3.14 What's New says 3-5% depending on platform and architecture, baseline Python 3.14 built with Clang 19 without the new interpreter). The original claim of 10% geomean, up to 40% on Python-heavy benchmarks (gist: 1.10x geomean, best 1.46x on scimark_sor, unpickle_list 1.02x slower) was artificially boosted by an LLVM 19 bug that slowed the computed-goto baseline.
corrections.workload: pyperformance suite, CPython built with clang-19, ThinLTO and PGO on AMD64 Ubuntu 22.04; per-benchmark results in gist https://gist.github.com/Fidget-Spinner/497c664eef389622d146d632990b0d21 (main 2228e92da31c vs tail-call 465467f47553, 2025-01-05).
corrections.caveats: Baseline is CPython itself, so this is a delta against the incumbent's previous dispatch, not against another implementation. The headline 10%/40% numbers were withdrawn by the authors after an LLVM 19 bug was found; the corrected 3-5% geomean is the figure to use, and even that baseline is the Clang 19 computed-goto build, which issue #158283 measures as 7.7% slower than a GCC 13 build on Linux x86-64 and 11.4% slower with Xcode 16.4 on macOS arm64 (merged dispatch jumps). An independent measurement by Nelson Elhage (blog.nelhage.com, snippet only, blocked here) found only 1.03x on a Raptor Lake i5-13500 and 1.00x on an Apple M1 against a clang-18 computed-goto build. Needs Clang 19+ on x86-64/AArch64 and PGO; opt-in via --with-tail-call-interp. Separately, Python 3.15 What's New reports 15-20% pyperformance geomean on Windows x86-64 with MSVC 18 (Visual Studio 18.1.1) versus the switch-case interpreter on an AMD Ryzen 7 5800X (chart in faster-cpython/ideas results/5800X-msvc.pgo2-vs-msvc.pgo.tc.svg), and the official Windows 64-bit binaries now use the tail-calling interpreter. CPU model absent for the clang claim, so the tier is C.

notes: Claims match the issue (10% geomean / up to 40%, then the correction notice to 3-5%) and the gist (1.10x geomean, best 1.46x). Shortcomings: first-party only, no CPU model, corrected 3-5% still measured against the LLVM 19-regressed computed-goto baseline, independent rerun shows 1.00-1.03x. License corrected to SPDX Python-2.0 (the LICENSE file is the PSF License Version 2 stack with BeOpen, CNRI and CWI agreements plus 0BSD for documentation code; Python-2.0 is the OSI-approved identifier), usability stays copyable; stars 77.5k and last commit 2026-10-06 confirmed.
